suggestions.quote: The pages lift off the desk and swirl round your head, every one you ever read, and with them the shout from when you were nine.
suggestions.fix: Draw the pages as blank or ruled paper-cut sheets with ink scribble lines, since only tags and bubbles may carry text. Show the nine-year-old shout as a crimson bubble of four words or fewer, or as a bare crimson jagged burst. Build it as one reusable page-swirl layer, so the swirl, the papered room and the settling at the end are a single code asset.

suggestions.quote: You snap at mom over something from years ago; she doesn't remember it at all.
suggestions.fix: Stage it as two side-on figures. Mom gets a bubble of four words or fewer, such as 'What? When was that?', followed by a puzzled-brow face reaction within 2 s. Keep your crimson shout bubble small and off both faces.

suggestions.quote: Every argument with everyone, kept for eighty years.
suggestions.fix: Avoid a new aged rig. Show it as a drifting stack of crimson bubble layers behind a time-lapse of your scarf and tuft greying, or a split-flap year counter. Name it as a new asset in the G2 script so it is not a surprise long pole. The same stack of layers can be reused from the papered-room set.

suggestions.quote: In the hall you recall the textbook page word for word, and the question asks you to apply it to something new: you freeze
suggestions.fix: The exam hall is a new set. Keep it to a flat row of desks as a drifting layer under the existing desk and lamp kit. The freeze uses a held pose with an afraid face and a pen drop, not a new prop. The word-for-word recall shows as the page swirl locking into rows, which needs no readable text.

suggestions.quote: The fact lands on you: what the research found when people with highly superior autobiographical memory took ordinary memory tests
suggestions.fix: Draw the finding as a paper diagram that draws itself, two bars against each other on the scene, then land it on you within two lines. Do not let this run as two fact lines in a row while the story stands still.

suggestions.quote: The desk at night, mom brings tea, you cram and mutter "I'll forget it all after anyway".
suggestions.fix: Name the rule device at G2. Suggested: the pages accumulate around you and stay in colour and in the room while the world around them fades to grey paper, so it applies in every scene. Also say which of you, mom and the pages stay in colour. Tag mood lines as `> MOOD: lamp` for the cram and the fear, and `> MOOD: night` for the hall.

suggestions.quote: The turn breaks "Forgetting is losing." : forgetting was how you two forgave each other.
suggestions.fix: Not a failed check, because G1 has no `cues.yaml`: it is not in my inputs, and I cannot check sound.md #1 or #3. At G2, write `cues.yaml` with a one-word intent per beat, such as clamour, then hush, then warm. Place the music-intent change at or after the spoken turn line, not before it. Use music in on the cycle memory and out on the final tea.

suggestions.quote: Mom brings tea; you take it, look up, and the pages settle on the desk.
suggestions.fix: In the last 15 s keep the right third quiet. Place you and mom left of centre, and keep the settling pages and the closing line inside the image on the left two-thirds.

keep.quote: You let one memory go, and take the tea she brings you
forgetting was how you two forgave each other
